title: [YouPass Collect] - Aging population trends across regions 2000-2050
prompt: The table below gives information about the population of people aged 60 and over in six regions in 2000 and the predicted figures for 2050. It also shows the world total of people aged 60 and over in 2000 and 2050. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table presents data on the percentage of elderly people aged 60 or older in six different regions, along with the global figure, in 2000, with forecasts for 2050.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the proportion of senior citizens is expected to rise in all regions over the 50-year period. Additionally, Europe consistently had the highest elderly population, while Asia is projected to experience the most substantial absolute growth.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Beginning with regions that had higher elderly populations initially, Europe recorded the highest figure at 22% in 2000, followed by Asia and North America at 12% and 11%, respectively, with Oceania at a similar level of 11%. By 2050, Europe's proportion is forecast to increase to 31%, maintaining its leading position. Meanwhile, Asia is expected to see the most dramatic rise among these regions, more than doubling to 28%, while North America's figure is projected to reach 26%. Oceania is also anticipated to double, ending at 22%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for regions with lower starting percentages, Latin America stood at 7% in 2000, while Africa had the smallest proportion at just 5%. Over the following five decades, Latin America's figure is predicted to more than double to 18%, whereas Africa's is expected to increase nearly two-and-a-half-fold to 12%. Finally, the worldwide percentage of elderly individuals was 13% in 2000 and is forecast to rise to 24% by 2050.
